title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Confirmatory Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured the effect of template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (plus limited automated repair) on validator acceptance of LLM-generated network configurations under adversarially crafted intents. The preregistered formal estimand was the paired difference in per-intent acceptance-for-deployment as judged by a deterministic validator (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). We executed the frozen plan on 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes=300; completed episodes=282; complete_pairs_included=141) with a single model (gpt-5-mini) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Observed complete-pair outcomes: baseline accepted 135/141 (95.7447%), guarded accepted 141/141 (100.0%); paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Interpreting the formal estimand (validator-accepted = success), the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable increase in validator-accepted configurations; archived traces show the six discordant pairs (n10=6) arose because sanitization/repair enabled acceptance where baseline lacked correction. The study is limited to synthetic intent templates, one model, one validator, and an unexecuted preregistered benign-control; these limitations and preregistration wording ambiguities are explicitly disclosed.

sections.introduction: LLM-based generation can translate high-level operator intent into device CLI, promising reduced manual effort but risking syntax, topology, and semantic errors and exposure to prompt-injection vectors. Prior work shows pairing generation with deterministic verification and repair reduces some error classes [1],[2],[3]. We ask: How effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating at preventing adversarially crafted intents from producing unsafe or policy-violating configurations in an LLM-driven NetOps pipeline? We contribute: (1) a preregistered confirmatory experiment (cand-2026-03) with a formal paired estimand measuring validator acceptance-for-deployment; (2) an artifact-backed analysis showing a small, statistically detectable change in per-intent acceptance between Baseline (LLM-only) and Guarded (sanitization + verifier-gating + limited repair) on synthetic adversarial intents; (3) an explicit reconciliation of a preregistration ambiguity and a concise failure analysis grounded in archived traces.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide rapid checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and are suitable validators for generate–validate pipelines [1],[2]. Recent NetOps experiments indicate LLMs produce useful drafts but commit syntax/semantic errors; incorporating verifier feedback and automated repair improves outcomes in prototype tasks [3]. Surveys and benchmarks emphasize fragmented evaluation practices and call for operational metrics beyond textual match [4],[5]. Security studies document prompt-injection risks motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses in operational pipelines [6]. Tool-augmented LM work (e.g., Toolformer) supports orchestrating external checks during generation [7]. Our study situates within generate–validate–repair literature and empirically evaluates verifier-gating and sanitization under a constrained adversary model.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. Study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The formal primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, with the per-intent binary outcome defined as 1 if the pipeline variant would accept a generated configuration for deployment as judged by the deterministic validator (validator-accepted = success). We explicitly resolve a preregistration ambiguity: the natural-language H1 used the phrase "reduce unsafe/attack acceptance," but the registered formal estimand and executed analysis measured validator acceptance-for-deployment; results are reported only against the formal estimand.
Design and interventions. Confirmatory paired design on N=150 adversarial intents (planned episodes=300). Conditions: Baseline = single-shot LLM generation (gpt-5-mini) whose initial candidate was recorded; Guarded = template-based input sanitization applied to the intent before generation and deterministic verifier-gating applied afterwards; the preregistered pipeline allowed at most one automated repair call per run under a frozen repair policy. Generation semantics were registered and implemented as shared_initial_candidate: the same initial generated candidate was used in both conditions where the shared stage applied; differences between Baseline and Guarded outcomes can therefore arise only from deterministic validation, sanitization, or the permitted repair stage, not from different first-pass sampling.
Execution and instrumentation. Declared components used as archived: generator = gpt-5-mini (provider field recorded as openai_responses), validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The task bank was synthetic intent templates covering interface admin, MTU, VLAN, static routes, and workflow constraints. Planned runs and missingness rules were applied: pairs excluded only when both paired runs were technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, or parser error). Provider-call and stage counts (shared_initial_generation and repair) are recorded in archived reconciliation artifacts.
sections.results: Execution summary. Planned episodes=300; completed episodes=282; failed episodes=18; model_calls_used=156. Primary confirmatory analysis used the 141 complete pairs (pairs with at least one scorable run). Observed outcomes on these 141 pairs: baseline_successes = 135 (135/141 = 0.9574468085106383); guarded_successes = 141 (141/141 = 1.0). Paired contingency (archived paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 (both accepted) = 135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 6; n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1) = 0; n00 = 0. Statistical inference. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test yields p = 0.03125. Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. Interpretation with formal estimand. Because the binary outcome equals deterministic-validator acceptance-for-deployment, the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable increase in validator-accepted configurations on the included pairs. Mechanism for discordant pairs. The six discordant n10 pairs correspond to cases where archived validator traces and repair logs show sanitizer and/or automated repair changed the candidate or its presentation to the validator and thereby enabled acceptance where the Baseline path lacked correction; the observed difference therefore arises from post-generation sanitization/repair and the validator gate, not from different initial sampled candidates (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Missingness-handling sensitivity (preregistered). Treating both-missing pairs (9 pairs where both runs failed) as failures (i.e., counting them as 0 for both conditions) yields baseline_successes = 135, guarded_successes = 141 over N=150 intents, so success rates become baseline = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded = 141/150 = 0.9400; paired difference = 0.04. The exact McNemar p remains 0.03125 because the discordant counts are unchanged; the bootstrap CI widens under this conservative treatment (archived sensitivity artifacts support this directionality). Unperformed preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M=50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed and are reported as unperformed preregistered items.
sections.discussion: Preregistration reconciliation and operational reading. We reconcile the preregistration wording by reporting results only against the archived formal estimand (validator-accepted = success). Under that estimand, the guarded pipeline increased validator acceptance by ≈4.25 percentage points on included pairs (p=0.03125); the six discordant cases reflect sanitizer/repair enabling acceptance rather than the gate rejecting otherwise unsafe outputs. Operational implications. In this constrained synthetic setting: (1) well-scoped sanitization and automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that an unguarded baseline fails to produce; (2) deterministic gating remains necessary to block invalid outputs, but gating policies should be designed jointly with repair/sanitization to avoid excessive false negatives (gates that only block can suppress potentially reparable valid candidates). Threats to validity. Construct validity: the validator encodes a limited set of safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants) and does not capture full protocol runtime semantics. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic intents, and single validator limit generalization to multi-vendor, protocol-diverse production networks. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective N; exclusion rules were preregistered and applied. Security coverage: the adversary model was limited to mutations of synthetic intents; broader prompt-injection vectors in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines remain for future work. Recommendations. Practitioners should pair generators with deterministic validators and tested repair routines, expand validator coverage toward protocol-level semantics, and jointly specify gating and repair policies before trusting automated deployment.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered confirmatory experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank shows that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and limited repair produced a small but statistically detectable increase in validator-accepted LLM-generated network configurations (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p=0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]) under the preregistered formal estimand (validator-accepted-for-deployment). The observed improvement arose from sanitizer/repair activity enabling acceptance in six discordant cases; it should not be read as a direct measurement of reduced attacker-success without an analysis that defines unsafe-acceptance as the estimand. Important limitations (synthetic tasks, single model and validator, and an unexecuted benign-control) constrain external claims. Future work must broaden validators, diversify models and vendors, run the preregistered benign-control and false-positive analyses, and evaluate defenses against richer prompt-injection threat models. Archived execution and analysis artifacts support the numeric claims reported here.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (provider field recorded as openai_responses), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Execution accounting (archived): planned episodes=300; completed episodes=282; failed episodes=18; complete_pairs used in primary analysis=141; model_calls_used=156. Outcome semantics: the preregistered formal estimand executed is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a per-intent binary "success" equals acceptance-for-deployment by the deterministic validator (validator-accepted = accepted). Note: a natural-language H1 in the preregistration discussed reducing attack/unsafe acceptance; we explicitly reconcile that ambiguity in the manuscript and report results only against the archived formal estimand. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Full run traces, tool-call logs, validator traces, and archived analysis artifacts are available in the submitted evidence bundle for machine verification; the Disclosure above intentionally omits per-file manifests and SHA-256 lists, which remain in the archive.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.

A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; we report and interpret results with respect to the archived formal estimand and explicitly disclose the phrasing ambiguity.
